reason: Conversation 1 gave the correct safety boundary (don't keep resetting, unplug, engineer to check) while also delivering an honest, well-hedged diagnosis: it tied the 'few minutes into 40/60 washes only' pattern to the heater element leaking to earth, correctly called for an insulation test before replacement, kept a control-board/wiring alternative open, and asked for the full model number before any part is named. Its second turn was marred by a boilerplate burning-smell warning that didn't match the customer's report (no smell, no sparks), but the substantive advice was sound. Conversation 2 gave only a bare stop/unplug instruction with no diagnosis, no questions about which device trips or whether it's heated-wash-only, and no escalation guidance beyond 'get it checked', leaving the homeowner with far less useful information.
